question: A 35 cm high bucket in the form of a frustum is full of water. Radii of its lower and upper ends are 12 cm and 18 cm, respectively. If water from this bucket is poured in a cylindrical drum, whose base radius is 20 cm, then what will be the height of water (in cm) in the drum?
solution:
**Given:**

The height of the frustum = 35 cm

The radius of the upper ends of the frustum = 12 cm

The radius of the lower ends of the frustum = 18 cm

The base radius of the cylindrical drum = 20 cm

**Formula used:**

The volume of the frustum = (πh/3) (R² + r² + Rr)

Where, h = The height of the frustum

R = Radius of the lower end

r = Radius of the upper end

The volume of a cylinder = πr²h

Where, r = Radius of the cylinder; h = Height of the cylinder

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1ccd00fea653d1103c0f82d6f9c84ada42d73ae12c6b2ec8115673eb0761a8db.png] 

Let, the height of water = x cm

So, [(22/7 × 35)/3] (182 + 122 + 18 × 12) = (22/7) × 202 × x

⇒ (110/3) (324 + 144 + 216) = (22/7) × 400x

⇒ (110/3) × 684 = (22/7) × 400x

⇒ 25080 = (22/7) × 400x

⇒ x = (25080 × 7)/(22 × 400) = 19.95

∴ The height of water (in cm) in the drum is 19.95 cm
